$comment: CORE-ONLY SIDECAR. Every other tests/fixtures/consensus-receipt.* file in this repo is BYTE-IDENTICAL to contract/src/__fixtures__/ in robotmoney-frontend — that byte identity IS the cross-repo pin (issue #1244 AC5), and it is asserted by .github/scripts/check_consensus_receipt_schema.py. This file is deliberately NOT part of that shared set: it carries the one thing the frontend structurally cannot, and adding it to a shared file would break the byte comparison that makes the pin checkable.
why_this_file_exists: consensus-receipt.canonicalization.json#digest_note names the keccak256 of the canonical bytes a CONSUMER OBLIGATION and explains why robotmoney-frontend cannot discharge it: contract/ has zero runtime and zero dev dependencies, and keccak256 is not reachable from a zero-dependency Bun test. node:crypto and Bun.CryptoHasher both offer sha3-256, which is NIST-padded and DIFFERENT (sha3-256("") is a7ffc6f8..., keccak256("") is c5d24601...), so it is not a substitute. robotmoney-core is the anchoring repo and has keccak256 available, so the obligation lands here. Tracked as robotmoney-core#1280.
derivation: keccak256 over the exact bytes of the named file, which are already domain-separated: the file's own first line is consensus-receipt.canonicalization.json#domain_separator. Nothing is prepended, appended, trimmed, or re-encoded — the trailing newline is part of the preimage.
not_transcribed: check_consensus_receipt_schema.py READS each file and HASHES it, then compares against the constant below. Changing the bytes without changing the constant fails, and changing the constant without changing the bytes fails. A constant that could only ever agree with itself is the failure mode robotmoney-core#1280 exists to prevent, and is exactly what the 1.0 draft's stale valid_fixture_digest was.

goldens.role: The payload_digest a consensusRecordReceipt call must carry for this fixture receipt.

The same, for the non-ASCII conformance receipt. Pinned separately because an ASCII-only digest check cannot detect a serializer that escapes non-ASCII, U+2028, or the HTML-sensitive characters — the two most likely non-JS implementations (Go's encoding/json, Python's json.dumps) each diverge that way BY DEFAULT while still reproducing an all-ASCII golden exactly.

still_open: robotmoney-core#1280 is now DISCHARGED IN FULL. The digest half is asserted here and in CI. The second half — that the anchoring path actually SUBMITS this digest for this fixture receipt — landed with the on-chain anchor in robotmoney-core#1247. Two independent assertions, at the two places the digest can go wrong: contracts/test/ConsensusRecommendationReceipt.t.sol (testAnchoringPathSubmitsTheGoldenDigest, testAnchoringPathSubmitsTheEscapingGoldenDigest) derives keccak256 from the golden file, compares it with the constant below, and asserts the same value is what ReceiptRecorded emits and what the contract stores; clients/rust-payment-client/tests/receipt.rs (submitted_calldata_carries_the_derived_digest_and_receipt_id, receipt_submit_anchors_the_pinned_digest_through_the_gateway) ABI-decodes the real consensusRecordReceipt calldata and asserts its payloadDigest argument equals this constant. Both read the constant out of THIS file at test time and compare it against a freshly derived hash, so changing either side alone still turns the suite red.

shared_fixture_manifest.purpose: THE CROSS-REPO PIN, IN ONE COMPARABLE VALUE (issue #1246). Every file below is byte-identical to contract/src/__fixtures__/<same name> in robotmoney-frontend. Neither repo's CI can fetch the other, so what makes that identity CHECKABLE rather than asserted is this manifest: either side re-hashes its own nine files and compares the list. A single differing sha256 names the drifted file.
shared_fixture_manifest.why_sha256_here_and_keccak256_above: keccak256 pins the goldens because that is what an EVM anchor computes. This manifest is aimed at the other repo, where contract/ has zero runtime and zero dev dependencies and cannot reach a keccak256 implementation at all — but sha256 is in its runtime (Bun.CryptoHasher, node:crypto). Pinning the shared set in sha256 is what lets the frontend check cross-repo identity with one command and no new dependency.
shared_fixture_manifest.not_transcribed: check_consensus_receipt_schema.py READS each file and HASHES it, then compares. Changing a shared fixture without changing its sha256 fails, and the reverse fails too.
shared_fixture_manifest.how_to_compare_from_robotmoney_frontend: cd contract/src/__fixtures__ && for f in $(...the nine names...); do printf '%s %s\n' "$f" "0x$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; done  — then diff against `files` below. A mismatch is a cross-repo drift and must be resolved by the release process in docs/product/20260623-product-proposal-investment-committee-v0.md §7.4, never by editing one side to match the other.
